```{r Notes}

## To Do List ##

# count number of inner wall only nests

# NN I 26 1a was a large pseudo until June 22, then a medium after
### REMEMBER to not count nests unfinished when we removed them at the end of summer. E.g., 70_5a had one cell built but shouldnt be considered the last cell




# excluded  nests that were eaten by birds or insect in parasite counts (neither parasitized or not)


### remove straw filled length when its not nessecary 

## Columns ##

# Nest_ID: the trapnest number, cavity number, and straw ID put together 
# Index: every row as a unique number that I needed for a loop
# Status: the activity of that cavity, e.g., its empty, new cells are made, a nest is sealed off, etc.
# Bee_choice: is a new nest built or not, Yes = 1, no = 0, pseudo nests or nests already in progress or completed get an NA.
# Available_post: number of available cavities for each trapnest and date combo AFTER the new nests for that visit have been started (i.e., how many available cavities that the experiments saw when arriving to the nest)
# New_nests_os: number of new osmia nests for each trapnest and date combo
# New_nests_meg: number of new megachile nests for each trapnest and date combo

# Osmia_ps_prior: the average number of osmia in each trapnest per date, prior to the number of new nests built that day, including pseudo nests
# Osmia_no_ps_prior: the average number of osmia in each trapnest per date, prior to the number of new nests built that day, excluding pseudo nests
# Meg_ps_prior: the average number of megachile in each trapnest per date, prior to the number of new nests built that day, including pseudo nests
# Meg_no_ps_prior: the average number of megachile in each trapnest per date, prior to the number of new nests built that day, excluding pseudo nests

# Osmia_ps_no_iw: the number of osmia in each trapnest per date, including new nests built that day, including pseudo nests, excluding only inner walls, for the parasite models (e.g., counting nests that a parasite could have infected)
# Osmia_no_ps_no_iw: the number of osmia in each trapnest per date, including new nests built that day, excluding pseudo nests, excluding only inner walls, for the parasite models
# Meg_ps_no_iw: the number of megachile in each trapnest per date, including new nests built that day, including pseudo nests, excluding only inner walls, for the parasite models
# Meg_no_ps_no_iw: the number of megachile in each trapnest per date, including new nests built that day, excluding pseudo nests, excluding only inner walls, for the parasite models

# New_nests_sum: total number of new nests including megachile and osmia.
# Available_cavities_prior: The number of cavities that were available for bees to nest in. E.g., if there are 2 new nests in a low-occupancy treatment, then there were 18 Available_cavities_prior, 2 new nests, and now 16 Available_post
# Available_post = Osmia_ps_prior + Meg_ps_prior (+ non-target nests) = 18


```

```{r Cleaning_2023}


knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE) 
library(sqldf)
library(tidyverse)
# citation() # to see package versions

# Load data
data_2023 <- read_csv('Data/Aggregate_nesting_data_2023.csv')

## Add in straws that remained empty throughout the experiment

# add empty data frame
empty_data_2023 <- read_csv('Data/Empty_data.csv')
# add columns to say 'for binding' or NA to tell data frames apart and prioritize the collected data
empty_data_2023$For_binding <- 0
data_2023$For_binding <- 1
# merge data frames
data_2023 <- bind_rows(empty_data_2023, data_2023)
# make nest ID column
data_2023$Nest_ID <- with(data_2023, paste(Trapnest, paste0(Cavity_number, Straw_ID), sep = '_'))
# make cavity ID column
data_2023$Cavity_ID <- with(data_2023, paste(Trapnest, Cavity_number, sep = '_'))
# make Trapnest a character
data_2023$Trapnest <- paste('trapnest', data_2023$Trapnest, sep = '_')

# to delete duplicate rows, check if it adds up
length(empty_data_2023$Straw_ID) # 1295 (minus one for the header)
# length(data$Straw_ID) data when first reading is 1110 (minus header)
sum(duplicated(data_2023$Nest_ID)) # 701 duplicates
# final data frame should be 1295+1110-701 = 1704
data_2023 <- data_2023 %>%
  group_by(Nest_ID) %>%
  filter(For_binding == max(For_binding))
length(data_2023$Nest_ID) # 1706, few extras.... ### CHECK ###


## Pivot longer and inspect
long_data_2023 <- pivot_longer(data_2023, '06-May':'09-Aug', names_to = 'Date', values_to = 'Status')
table(long_data_2023$Status)
table(long_data_2023$Occupant)
# Replace some input for statuses of how they should be treated
long_data_2023$Status <- replace(long_data_2023$Status, long_data_2023$Status == 'eaten', 'empty')
long_data_2023$Status <- replace(long_data_2023$Status, long_data_2023$Status == 'inner wall started', 'empty')
long_data_2023$Status <- replace(long_data_2023$Status, long_data_2023$Status == 'non-target inner wall started', 'empty')


## Make the date column actually a date
# divide Date column from day-month into two columns
long_data_2023 <- long_data_2023 %>%
  separate(Date, c('day', 'month'))
# inspect
table(long_data_2023$day)
table(long_data_2023$month)
# replace month names
long_data_2023$month <- replace(long_data_2023$month, long_data_2023$month == 'Jun', 'June')
long_data_2023$month <- replace(long_data_2023$month, long_data_2023$month == 'Aug', 'August')
long_data_2023$month <- replace(long_data_2023$month, long_data_2023$month == 'Jul', 'July')
# make new column with months as numbers
long_data_2023$month2 <- match(long_data_2023$month, month.name)
# add column for the year
long_data_2023 <- long_data_2023 %>% mutate(Year = 2023)
# make a column with the full date that is read by R as a date
long_data_2023$Date <- as.Date(with(long_data_2023, paste(Year, month2, day, sep = '-')), '%Y-%m-%d')
# check if R recognizes it as a date
str(long_data_2023)


## Fixing the Occupant column
# at first, this column says the occupant for the entire data collection period, even if the nest if empty for most of it
# make a new column, needs to ne 'NA' of loop wont run
long_data_2023 <- long_data_2023 %>% mutate(Occupant.v2 = ifelse(Status == 'non_existent', 'NA', ifelse(Status == 'empty', 'none', Occupant)))
long_data_2023 <- long_data_2023 %>% mutate(Occupant.v3 = ifelse(Status == 'no_visit', 'NA', Occupant.v2))
# add occupant for pseudo nests, Osmia first half of summer, Megachile second half
long_os <- long_data_2023 %>%
  filter(Site == 'NN' | Subsite == 'A' | Subsite == 'B' | Subsite == 'C' | Subsite == 'D' | Subsite == 'E' | Subsite == 'F') %>%
  mutate(Occupant.v3 = ifelse(Status == 'pseudo', 'osmia', Occupant.v3))
# add megachile for pseudo nest type
long_meg <- long_data_2023 %>%
  filter(Site == 'CP' | Subsite == 'M' | Subsite == 'N' | Subsite == 'O' | Subsite == 'P' | Subsite == 'Q' | Subsite == 'R') %>%
  mutate(Occupant.v3 = ifelse(Status == 'pseudo', 'megachile', Occupant.v3))
# merge back together
long_data_2023 <- rbind(long_os, long_meg)
# Take columns that I want
long_data_2023 <- long_data_2023 %>% select(Site:Straw_ID, Straw_length_mm, Filled_length_mm, Nest_ID, Cavity_ID, Occupant.v3, Date, Status)
# rename new occupant.v2 column
long_data_2023 <- rename(long_data_2023, Occupant = Occupant.v3)

# check if each trapnest has 18 existing cavities (unique cavity IDs) for each visit
long_data_2023 %>%
  filter(Status != 'non_existent' & Status != 'no_visit') %>%
  group_by(Trapnest, Date) %>%
  summarize(Count = length(unique(Nest_ID)))

# remove chunks of 'non_existent' for first and second half of the summer so the loop runs faster
# for the first half of the summer, BP and NN had different chunks of non_existents, so there's separate lists of data for them. But for the second half, CP and BP had the same dates so there's one list
long_data_BP_2023 <- long_data_2023 %>% filter(Subsite == 'A' | Subsite == 'B' | Subsite == 'C' | Subsite == 'D' | Subsite == 'E' | Subsite == 'F')
long_data_NN_2023 <- long_data_2023 %>% filter(Subsite == 'G' | Subsite == 'H' | Subsite == 'I' | Subsite == 'J' | Subsite == 'K' | Subsite == 'L')
long_data_BP_2023 <- long_data_BP_2023 %>% filter(Date != '2023-05-06' & Date != '2023-06-30' & Date != '2023-07-03' & Date != '2023-07-04' & Date != '2023-07-05' & Date != '2023-07-06' & Date != '2023-07-07' & Date != '2023-07-10' & Date != '2023-07-12' & Date != '2023-07-14' & Date != '2023-07-17' & Date != '2023-07-20' & Date != '2023-07-24' & Date != '2023-07-26' & Date != '2023-07-28' & Date != '2023-07-29' & Date != '2023-08-01' & Date != '2023-08-04' & Date != '2023-08-09')
long_data_NN_2023 <- long_data_NN_2023 %>% filter(Date != '2023-07-07' & Date != '2023-07-10' & Date != '2023-07-12' & Date != '2023-07-14' & Date != '2023-07-17' & Date != '2023-07-20' & Date != '2023-07-24' & Date != '2023-07-26' & Date != '2023-07-28' & Date != '2023-07-29' & Date != '2023-08-01' & Date != '2023-08-04' & Date != '2023-08-09')
long_data_second_2023 <- long_data_2023 %>% filter(Subsite == 'M' | Subsite == 'N' | Subsite == 'O' | Subsite == 'P' | Subsite == 'Q' | Subsite == 'R' | Subsite == 'S' | Subsite == 'T' | Subsite == 'U' | Subsite == 'V' | Subsite == 'W' | Subsite == 'X')
long_data_second_2023 <- long_data_second_2023 %>% filter(Date != '2023-05-06' & Date != '2023-05-07' & Date != '2023-05-11' & Date != '2023-05-12' & Date != '2023-05-15' & Date != '2023-05-16' & Date != '2023-05-17' & Date != '2023-05-18' & Date != '2023-05-19' & Date != '2023-05-21' & Date != '2023-05-22' & Date != '2023-05-23' & Date != '2023-05-25' & Date != '2023-05-26' & Date != '2023-05-28' & Date != '2023-05-29' & Date != '2023-05-31' & Date != '2023-06-01' & Date != '2023-06-02' & Date != '2023-06-04' & Date != '2023-06-05' & Date != '2023-06-08' & Date != '2023-06-09' & Date != '2023-06-10' & Date != '2023-06-11' & Date != '2023-06-12' & Date != '2023-06-14' & Date != '2023-06-15' & Date != '2023-06-16' & Date != '2023-06-19' & Date != '2023-06-20' & Date != '2023-06-22' & Date != '2023-06-23' & Date != '2023-06-29' & Date != '2023-06-30')

long_data_2023 <- rbind(long_data_BP_2023, long_data_NN_2023, long_data_second_2023) # 15180 + 18486 + 13124 = 46790


## Loop for making the column for new nests per visit at the cavity-level

# make an index
index_2023 <- (1:length(long_data_2023$Site)) # make index of 1 to last row
long_i_2023 <- long_data_2023
long_i_2023$index <- index_2023 # making index column to count
long_i_2023 <- long_i_2023 %>% relocate('index') # puts it in the front
# initialize a table for bee choice
Bee_choice_2023 <- as.data.frame(matrix(NA,0,2))
colnames(Bee_choice_2023)[1] <- 'index'
colnames(Bee_choice_2023)[2]<-'Bee_choice'
# saying for i in each of the rows in index

### START
for (i in long_i_2023$index) { 
  # make an i-1 and i-2 and i-3 variable
  i_status <- long_i_2023$Status[i]
  i_minus_one_status <- long_i_2023$Status[i-1]
  i_minus_two_status <- long_i_2023$Status[i-2]
  i_minus_three_status <- long_i_2023$Status[i-3]
  # initialize a choice variable
  choice <- 'blank'
  
  if(i_status == 'non_existent' | i_status == 'no change' | i_status == 'no_visit' | i_status == 'pseudo') {
    choice <- 'NA'
  }else{
    if(i_status == 'empty'){
      choice <- '0'
      }else{
        if(i_status != 'non_existent' & i_status != 'no change' & i_status != 'no_visit' & i_status != 'pseudo' & i_status != 'empty' & i_minus_one_status == 'non_existent' | i_minus_one_status == 'empty') {
        choice <- '1'
      }else{
        if(i_status != 'non_existent' & i_status != 'no change' & i_status != 'no_visit' & i_status != 'pseudo' & i_status != 'empty' & i_minus_one_status == 'no_visit' & i_minus_two_status == 'non_existent' | i_minus_two_status == 'empty') {
          choice <- '1'
        }else{ 
          if(i_status != 'non_existent' & i_status != 'no change' & i_status != 'no_visit' & i_status != 'pseudo' & i_status != 'empty' & i_minus_one_status != 'non_existent' | i_minus_one_status != 'empty') {
          choice <- 'NA' 
          }else{
            if(i_status != 'non_existent' & i_status != 'no change' & i_status != 'no_visit' & i_status != 'pseudo' & i_status != 'empty' & i_minus_one_status == 'no_visit' & i_minus_two_status != 'non_existent' & i_minus_two_status != 'empty') {
            choice <- 'NA'
            }else{ 
              if(i_status != 'non_existent' & i_status != 'no change' & i_status != 'no_visit' & i_status != 'pseudo' & i_status != 'empty' & i_minus_one_status == 'no_visit' & i_minus_two_status == 'no_visit' & i_minus_three_status != 'non_existent' & i_minus_three_status != 'empty') {choice <- 'leftover'}
              else{ 
                choice <- 'leftover'}
      }}}}}}

  occupant_i <- long_i_2023$Occupant[i]
  if(occupant_i == 'wasp' | occupant_i == 'hylaeus' | occupant_i == 'resin bee' | occupant_i == 'heriades' | occupant_i == 'hoplitis'){
    choice <- 'NA'
  } else {choice <- choice}

  # create Bee_choice row for our big table
  Bee_choice_i <- as.data.frame(matrix(NA,0,2))
  colnames(Bee_choice_i)[1] <- 'index'
  colnames(Bee_choice_i)[2] <- 'Bee_choice'
  Bee_choice_i[nrow(Bee_choice_i)+1,] = c(i,choice)
  # bind the row to the big table
  Bee_choice_2023 <- rbind(Bee_choice_2023, Bee_choice_i)
} ### END

# Join products together
Bee_choice_2023$index <- as.numeric(Bee_choice_2023$index)
long_choice_2023 <- long_i_2023 %>% left_join(Bee_choice_2023)
long_choice_2023$Bee_choice <- as.numeric(long_choice_2023$Bee_choice)

# Inspect new nests
sum(long_choice_2023$Bee_choice, na.rm = TRUE) # 264 new nests, but this is incorrect, we had fewer nests, are there duplicates?
inspect_2023_new_nest <- long_choice_2023 %>% filter(Bee_choice == 1)
# some duplicates, like 5_9a, 6_17a, 7_3a, 29_1b
length(unique(inspect_2023_new_nest$Nest_ID)) # 226 unique nests, that makes more sense
# show the duplicates
inspect_2023_new_nest %>%
  group_by(Nest_ID) %>%
  filter(n() > 1) %>%
  arrange(Nest_ID)
# there does not seem to be a pattern for why these nest are being counted twice in the loop, so manually remove the duplicates
# remove duplicates by arranging by date first, then replace with NA
long_choice_2023 <- long_choice_2023 %>%
  arrange(Nest_ID, Date) %>% 
  group_by(Nest_ID) %>%
  mutate(Bee_choice = ifelse(
    Bee_choice == 1 & duplicated(Bee_choice == 1), 
    NA, 
    Bee_choice)) %>%
  ungroup()
# check the sum
sum(long_choice_2023$Bee_choice, na.rm = TRUE) 
# 226, perfect

table(long_choice_2023$Occupant[long_choice_2023$Bee_choice == 1])


```

```{r Cleaning_2024}
 

## Load data
data_2024 <- read_csv('Data/Aggregate_nesting_data_2024.csv')

# make nest ID column
data_2024$Nest_ID <- with(data_2024, paste(Trapnest, paste0(Cavity_number, Straw_ID), sep = '_'))
# make cavity ID column
data_2024$Cavity_ID <- with(data_2024, paste(Trapnest, Cavity_number, sep = '_'))
# make Trapnest a character
data_2024$Trapnest <- paste('trapnest', data_2024$Trapnest, sep = '_')

## Pivot longer and inspect

table(long_data_2024$Status) 
table(long_data_2024$Occupant) 
# Replace some input for statuses of how they should be treated
long_data_2024$Status <- replace(long_data_2024$Status, long_data_2024$Status=='eaten','empty')
long_data_2024$Status <- replace(long_data_2024$Status, long_data_2024$Status=='inner wall started','empty')
long_data_2024$Status <- replace(long_data_2024$Status, long_data_2024$Status=='non-target inner wall started','empty')
long_data_2024$Status <- replace(long_data_2024$Status, long_data_2024$Status=='activity','no change') # meant there was some new material in the nest but didn't change the overall status (e.g., more pollen added to the same cell as last time)
long_data_2024$Status <- replace(long_data_2024$Status, long_data_2024$Status=='end chewed','empty') # megachile would chew the ends of the straws, so we would replace them with new ones


## Make the date column actually a date

long_data_2024$month <- replace(long_data_2024$month, long_data_2024$month == 'Jul', 'July')

## Fixing the Occupant column

# rename new occupant.v2 column

  arrange(Nest_ID, Date) %>% 
  group_by(Nest_ID) %>%
  mutate(Bee_choice = ifelse(
    Bee_choice == 1 & duplicated(Bee_choice == 1), 
    NA, 
    Bee_choice)) %>%
  ungroup()
# check the sum
sum(long_choice_2024$Bee_choice, na.rm = TRUE) 
# check only megachile and osmia have new nests counted
table(long_choice_2024$Occupant[long_choice_2024$Bee_choice == 1])


```

```{r Nests_Containing_Cells_2023}
 

## Categorize occupied nests as containing cells, or as just inner walls


# make column to say if the Status contains the word 'cell' (1) or not (0)
contains_cells_2023 <- long_choice_2023 %>% filter(Status != 'empty' & Status != 'pseudo' & Occupant == 'osmia' | Status != 'empty' & Status != 'pseudo' & Occupant == 'megachile')
contains_cells_2023$Contains_cells_bin <- ifelse(grepl('cell', contains_cells_2023$Status), 1, 0) 


# Loop to say nests contained cells for the duration they remained in the trapnest

# arrange data chronologically
contains_cells_2023 <- contains_cells_2023 %>% arrange(Nest_ID, Date)
# initiate new column, then fill it in
contains_cells_2023$Contains_cells_cumulative <- contains_cells_2023$Contains_cells_bin 


### START
for(i in 1:nrow(contains_cells_2023)){
  nestID <- contains_cells_2023$Nest_ID[i] # focal nest for i-th row
  dt <- contains_cells_2023$Date[i] # date for i-th row
  allprev <- contains_cells_2023 %>% filter(Nest_ID == nestID & Date <= dt) %>% pull(Contains_cells_cumulative) #  previous counts for that focal nest
  
  check1 <- !all(is.na(allprev))

  if(check1){
    contains_cells_2023$Contains_cells_cumulative[i] <- max(allprev, na.rm = T)
  }
} ### END

# remove unnecessary columns
contains_cells_2023 <- contains_cells_2023 %>% select(-Contains_cells_bin)
# rename column and df
contains_cells_2023 <- contains_cells_2023 %>% rename(Contains_cells = Contains_cells_cumulative)

# merge with prefs

long_choice_2023 <- full_join(long_choice_2023, contains_cells_2023)
long_choice_2023 <- long_choice_2023 %>% arrange(Nest_ID, Date)

```

```{r Available_Cavities_Post_2023}
 

## Count the number of Available Cavities in each trapnest after the new nests for that visit

# make a new column to say available (1) or not (0), or NA
long_avail_2023 <- long_choice_2023 %>% 
  mutate(Available_bin = ifelse(Status == 'no_visit' | Status == 'non_existent', NA, ifelse(Status == 'empty', 1,  0))) 
# make a summary column to say the number of available nests in each trapnest by date AFTER that visit's bees began nesting
summ_avail_2023 <- long_avail_2023 %>% 
  group_by(Trapnest, Date) %>% 
  summarize(Available_post = sum(Available_bin, na.rm = T))
# the zeros are no_visits, so replace zeros with NA
summ_avail_2023$Available_post <- replace(summ_avail_2023$Available_post, summ_avail_2023$Available_post == 0, NA)
# Available_post: number of available cavities for each trapnest and date combo after new nests had been built, i.e., the number of available cavities we saw on that visit


```

```{r Conspecific_Presence_for_Bee_Models_2023}
# includes inner walls only as conspecifics

### Nesting according to conspecific presence (with and without pseudo nests) ###

## Osmia ##

# Make column to say osmia present or not, including pseudo
conspecifics_os_2023 <- long_choice_2023 %>% 
  mutate(Osmia_bi_ps = ifelse(Occupant == 'osmia', 1, 0))  

# Make column to say osmia present or not, excluding pseudo
conspecifics_os_2023 <- conspecifics_os_2023 %>% 
  mutate(Osmia_bi_no_ps = ifelse(Occupant == 'osmia' & Status != 'pseudo', 1, 0)) 

## Count the number of osmia in each nest

# with pseudo nests/ pseudo nests considered osmia occupancies
summ_osmia_ps_2023 <- conspecifics_os_2023 %>% 
  group_by(Trapnest, Date) %>% 
  summarize(Osmia_ps = (sum(Osmia_bi_ps)))
# Osmia_ps: number of osmia in each trapnest per date, including pseudo nests

# without pseudo nests (pseudo nests not considered osmia occupancies)
summ_osmia_no_ps_2023 <- conspecifics_os_2023 %>% 
  group_by(Trapnest, Date) %>% 
  summarize(Osmia_no_ps = (sum(Osmia_bi_no_ps)))
# Osmia_no_ps: number of osmia in each trapnest per date, excluding pseudo nests

# Merge together
conspecifics_os_2_2023 <- merge(conspecifics_os_2023,  summ_osmia_ps_2023, all.x = TRUE)
conspecifics_os_2_2023 <- merge(conspecifics_os_2_2023,  summ_osmia_no_ps_2023, all.x = TRUE)

# Delete columns I dont need
conspecifics_os_2_2023 <- conspecifics_os_2_2023 %>% select(-Osmia_bi_ps, -Osmia_bi_no_ps )


## Megachile ##

# Make column to say osmia present or not, including pseudo
conspecifics_meg_2023 <- long_choice_2023 %>% 
  mutate(Mega_bi_ps = ifelse(Occupant == 'megachile', 1, 0)) 

# Make column to say osmia present or not, excluding pseudo
conspecifics_meg_2023 <- conspecifics_meg_2023 %>% 
  mutate(Mega_bi_no_ps = ifelse(Occupant == 'megachile' & Status != 'pseudo', 1, 0)) 

## Count the number of genera in each nest

# with pseudo nests/ pseudo nests considered osmia occupancies
summ_meg_ps_2023 <- conspecifics_meg_2023 %>% 
  group_by(Trapnest, Date) %>% 
  summarize(Meg_ps = (sum(Mega_bi_ps)))
# Meg_ps: number of megachile in each trapnest per date, including pseudo nests

# without pseudo nests/ pseudo nests not considered osmia occupancies
summ_meg_no_ps_2023 <- conspecifics_meg_2023 %>% 
  group_by(Trapnest, Date) %>% 
  summarize(Meg_no_ps = (sum(Mega_bi_no_ps)))
# Meg_no_ps: number of megachile in each trapnest per date, excluding pseudo nests

# Merge together
conspecifics_meg_2_2023 <- merge(conspecifics_meg_2023,  summ_meg_ps_2023, all.x = TRUE)
conspecifics_meg_2_2023 <- merge(conspecifics_meg_2_2023,  summ_meg_no_ps_2023, all.x = TRUE)

# Delete columns I dont need
conspecifics_meg_2_2023 <- conspecifics_meg_2_2023 %>% select(-Mega_bi_ps, -Mega_bi_no_ps )

# Join Osmia and Megachile data together
conspecifics_both_1_2023 <- merge(conspecifics_os_2_2023, conspecifics_meg_2_2023)


```

```{r Counting_New_Nests_2023}
## Counting the number of new nests

  filter(Bee_choice == 1 & Occupant == 'osmia') %>%  
  group_by(Trapnest, Date) %>%
  summarize(New_nests_os = sum(Bee_choice == 1))

  filter(Bee_choice == 1 & Occupant ==  'megachile') %>%

  summarize(New_nests_meg = sum(Bee_choice == 1))

conspecifics_and_avail_2023 <- inner_join(conspecifics_2023, summ_avail_2023) 
new_nests_os_2023 <- full_join(conspecifics_and_avail_2023, summ_new_os_2023)
```

```{r Calculating_Prior_Values}
 

## Changing occupant count for prior number to be the average number of congenera 

# When I'm looking at bee preferences, I need the values prior to the bee deciding to build her nest. E.g., how many nests existed when the bee decided to establish her nest.
# When I'm looking at parasite density, I need the total values, not the prior values. E.g., how many existing nests are there in a trapnest when a parasite decides to lay an egg

# need to make theses columns the number of occupencies PRIOR to the bee nesting, e.g., the new nests should not count in Osmia_ps and Osmia_no_ps
# If theres 1 new nest, make new column to say Osmia_(no_)ps - New_nests_os
# If there are multiple nests, to take the average, do ((n-1)/2) + (Osmia_ps - New_nests_os), n being the number of new nests per genera. Osmia_ps if the total count of osmia in the trapnest, not the prior count
# e.g., 1 new nest, 9 Osmia_ps = 9-1 = 8
# e.g, 3 new nests, 9 Osmia_ps (so only 6 were filled the previous visit) = ((3-1)/2) + (9-3) = 7
# Osmia_ps_prior + Available_prior should usually = 18, unless there's non-target occupants

# 1- for 0 or 1 new nests, (available_post - new nests) 
  # osmia pseudo 
preferences_1 <- preferences_1 %>% mutate(Osmia_ps_prior_V1 = ifelse(New_nests_os == 1 | New_nests_os == 0, (Osmia_ps - New_nests_os), 'TBD'))
  # osmia no pseudo
preferences_1 <- preferences_1 %>% mutate(Osmia_no_ps_prior_V1 = ifelse(New_nests_os == 1 | New_nests_os == 0, (Osmia_no_ps - New_nests_os), 'TBD'))
  # megachile pseudo
preferences_1 <- preferences_1 %>% mutate(Meg_ps_prior_V1 = ifelse(New_nests_meg == 1 | New_nests_meg == 0, (Meg_ps - New_nests_meg), 'TBD'))
  # megachile no pseudo
preferences_1 <- preferences_1 %>% mutate(Meg_no_ps_prior_V1 = ifelse(New_nests_meg == 1 | New_nests_meg == 0, (Meg_no_ps - New_nests_meg), 'TBD'))

# 2 A- for multiple new nests, (n-1)/2
  # osmia
preferences_1 <- preferences_1 %>% mutate(Osmia_equ = ifelse(New_nests_os > 1, ((New_nests_os - 1)/2), NA))
  # megachile
preferences_1 <- preferences_1 %>% mutate(Meg_equ = ifelse(New_nests_meg > 1, ((New_nests_meg - 1)/2), NA))

# B- add equation + (available_post - new nests)
  # osmia pseudo
preferences_1 <- preferences_1 %>% mutate(Osmia_ps_prior = ifelse(Osmia_ps_prior_V1 == 'TBD', (Osmia_equ + Osmia_ps - New_nests_os), ifelse(is.na(Osmia_equ) & !is.na(Osmia_ps_prior_V1) | Osmia_ps_prior_V1 != 'TBD', Osmia_ps_prior_V1, 'leftover' )))
  # osmia no pseudo
preferences_1 <- preferences_1 %>% mutate(Osmia_no_ps_prior = ifelse(Osmia_no_ps_prior_V1 == 'TBD', (Osmia_equ + Osmia_no_ps - New_nests_os), ifelse(is.na(Osmia_equ) & !is.na(Osmia_no_ps_prior_V1) | Osmia_no_ps_prior_V1 != 'TBD', Osmia_no_ps_prior_V1, 'leftover' )))
  # megachile pseudo
preferences_1 <- preferences_1 %>% mutate(Meg_ps_prior = ifelse(Meg_ps_prior_V1 == 'TBD', (Meg_equ + Meg_ps - New_nests_meg), ifelse(is.na(Meg_equ) & !is.na(Meg_ps_prior_V1) | Meg_ps_prior_V1 != 'TBD', Meg_ps_prior_V1, 'leftover' ))) 
  # megachile no pseudo
preferences_1 <- preferences_1 %>% mutate(Meg_no_ps_prior = ifelse(Meg_no_ps_prior_V1 == 'TBD', (Meg_equ + Meg_no_ps - New_nests_meg), ifelse(is.na(Meg_equ) & !is.na(Meg_no_ps_prior_V1) | Meg_no_ps_prior_V1 != 'TBD', Meg_no_ps_prior_V1, 'leftover' )))

# take only columns I need
preferences <- preferences_1 %>% select(Date, Site, Subsite, Treatment, Trapnest, Cavity_number, Straw_ID, Cavity_size, Filled_length_mm, Straw_length_mm, Nest_ID, Cavity_ID, Status, Contains_cells, Occupant, Good_days, Bee_choice, Available_post, New_nests_os, New_nests_meg, Osmia_ps, Osmia_no_ps, Meg_ps, Meg_no_ps, Osmia_ps_prior, Osmia_no_ps_prior, Meg_ps_prior, Meg_no_ps_prior, Osmia_ps_no_iw, Osmia_no_ps_no_iw, Meg_ps_no_iw, Meg_no_ps_no_iw)

# since I'm looking at new nests, I'm not going to make the other colums like osmia_ps_prior etc 'NA' is Bee-choice is NA, because there shouldnt be a time where I'm using those values if Bee_choice isn't 1 or 0

```

```{r Available_Cavities_Prior}

# Sum the megachile and osmia nests on the same day
# if one column is NA and the other isn't, put the column that isn't NA, but if there's values in both, add them together
preferences <- preferences %>% mutate(New_nests_sum = ifelse(!is.na(New_nests_os) & is.na(New_nests_meg), New_nests_os, ifelse(is.na(New_nests_os) & !is.na(New_nests_meg), New_nests_meg, (New_nests_os + New_nests_meg))))

preferences <- preferences %>% mutate(Available_cavities_prior = Available_post + New_nests_sum)
```

```{r Emergence_Wrangling}

# nesting_cells is the nesting data with cell-level observations

# Columns 
 # Cumulative_par: cumulative number of parasites for that specific nest. E.g., 6_15a had no parasites when 1 cell was built, then two more cells each had a parasite, then six more cells with three parasites. So cumulative_par is 0, 2, then 5, and 5 until the nest is removed 
 # Number_of_cells: the cumulative number of cells in the nest at the time. Comes from parasite data
 # Cell_parasitized: if that cell is parasitized, binary
# NOTE: some columns have duplicated data after merging, eg., multiple 1s for Bee_choice or duplicated straw length and filled length


### Question 3: Do parasites affect nesting preferences ###

# load data
emergence_2023 <- read_csv('Data/Emergence_data_2023.csv')  
emergence_2024 <- read_csv('Data/Emergence_data_2024.csv')  

# inspect
table(emergence_2023$Cell_occupant)
table(emergence_2024$Cell_occupant)


## Merge dfs and wrangle cell_number and cell_position, and create cell_parasitized  

# make column to turn cell number into cell position for emergence_2023
# take max number of each nest
emergence_2023 <- emergence_2023 %>%
  arrange(Nest_ID, Date) %>%
  group_by(Nest_ID) %>%
  mutate(Cell_position_2 = if_else(Cell_number == max(Cell_number), 'last cell', 'not last cell')) %>%
  ungroup()

# merge together the two Cell_position columns and rename for 2023 data
emergence_2023 <- emergence_2023 %>%
  mutate(Cell_position_combined = coalesce(Cell_position, Cell_position_2))
emergence_2023 <- emergence_2023 %>% select(-Cell_position, -Cell_position_2)
emergence_2023 <- emergence_2023 %>% rename(Cell_position = Cell_position_combined)

# NOTE: the cell_number column does not always indicate the order of cells built, especially if there are multiple built on the same day. It's a way to distinguish the cell-level data. What's imrpotant is the date each cell was built, and weather its the last cell or not (Cell_position)


## Make a cell number column for 2024 data, and fill in the blanks for the 2023 data

# add in the ascending number
emergence_2024 <- emergence_2024 %>%
  arrange(Nest_ID, Date) %>% 
  group_by(Nest_ID) %>% 
  mutate(Cell_number = row_number())

emergence_2023 <- emergence_2023 %>%
  arrange(Nest_ID, Date) %>% 
  group_by(Nest_ID) %>%
  mutate(
    Cell_number = if_else(
      is.na(Cell_number), 
      row_number(),
      Cell_number)) %>%
  ungroup()

# bind dfs together
emergence <- bind_rows(emergence_2023, emergence_2024)
length(emergence_2023$Site) + length(emergence_2024$Site) # = length(emergence$Site) 

# make cell ID column
emergence$Cell_ID <- with(emergence, paste(Nest_ID, Cell_number, sep = '_'))

# rearrange and remove columns I don't need
emergence <- emergence %>% select(Site, Subsite, Trapnest, Treatment, Cavity_size, Cavity_number, Straw_ID, Nest_ID, Cell_number, Cell_ID, Cell_position, Date, Cell_occupant,  Species_or_subtype)


## Filter out non-target occupants

  # first, straight from the emergence data
non_target <- c('heriades', 'hoplitis', 'hyleaus', 'masked bee', 'non-target bee', 'NA', 'resin bee', 'wasp', 'unknown')
emergence <- emergence %>%
  group_by(Nest_ID) %>%
  filter(!any(Cell_occupant %in% non_target)) %>%  
  ungroup()
table(emergence$Cell_occupant)


  # second, remove from the emergence data again, but using the occupant column in preferences (to catch nests that didn't develope enough to emerge, but we know based on their nesting material from the field data)
table(preferences$Occupant)
nests_to_remove <- preferences %>% 
  filter(Occupant %in% non_target) %>% 
  pull(Nest_ID) %>%
  unique()
emergence <- emergence %>%
  filter(!Nest_ID %in% nests_to_remove)

  # finally, filter out the non-target occupants in the preferences data
preferences <- preferences %>% filter(Occupant == 'osmia' | Occupant =='megachile' | Occupant == 'none')


## Wrangle number of cells and parasites

# create column to say if cell is parasitized or not
table(emergence$Cell_occupant)
emergence <- emergence %>% 
  mutate(Cell_parasitized = ifelse(Cell_occupant == 'parasite', 1, 0))

# take number of cells total for that nest and date combo
emergence <- emergence %>% 
    group_by(Nest_ID, Date) %>% 
    mutate(Number_of_cells = max(Cell_number))

# check that each nest has only one type of bee, e.g., not mislabelled 
emergence %>%
  group_by(Nest_ID) %>%
  summarise(Occupants = paste(unique(Cell_occupant), collapse = ', '),
      .groups = 'drop')


## Make column to say nest is parasitized or not for when a parasite is in a cell, from that date onwards

# make column to say for each date, if a cell has parasites, then count cumulative parasites in a new column
emergence <- emergence %>% 
  arrange(Nest_ID, Date) %>% 
  group_by(Nest_ID) %>% 
  mutate(Cumulative_par = cumsum(Cell_parasitized))

# take max number of parasites for a nest_ID - date combo
# e.g., on 2023-06-14 for 13_18a (cells 1 and 2), both are parasitized, so take the highest parasite count for that date, so say for 13_18a on 2023-06-14, there's 2 parasites
emergence <- emergence %>% 
  group_by(Date, Nest_ID) %>% 
  mutate(Cumulative_par_max = max(Cumulative_par)) %>% 
  ungroup()


## Bind emergence and preferences data 

# preferences has one row per nest and date, while emergence data has multiple rows per date (one per cell)
emergence$Trapnest <- paste('trapnest', emergence$Trapnest, sep = '_')
emerg_and_pref <- full_join(emergence, preferences) 


## Inspect

 # check for Date mismatches

setdiff(emergence$Date, preferences$Date) # no Dates are in emergence but not in preferences
setdiff(preferences$Date, emergence$Date) # some dates are in preferences but not emergence because we visited the field but don't have emergence data for that day (e.g., only non-target activity or no field activity)


 # check for Nest_ID mismatches

setdiff(emergence$Nest_ID, preferences$Nest_ID)  # IDs in emergence but not in preferences: 
  # 18_8b: must be mislabelled, remove
emerg_and_pref <- emerg_and_pref %>% filter(Nest_ID != '18_8b')

# see below for IDs in preferences but not in emergence
# compare the nest IDs in the dfs of nests with activity

# nest_IDs_preferences <- preferences %>%
#   filter(Status != 'pseudo' & Status != 'empty' & Status != 'no change' & Bee_choice == 1 & Contains_cells == 1) %>%
#   group_by(Nest_ID) %>%
#   ungroup() %>%
#   arrange(Nest_ID)
# nest_IDs_preferences <- nest_IDs_preferences %>% select(Nest_ID)
# 
# nest_IDs_emergence <- emergence %>%
#   group_by(Nest_ID) %>%
#   slice(1) %>%
#   ungroup() %>%
#   arrange(Nest_ID)
# nest_IDs_emergence <- nest_IDs_emergence %>% select(Nest_ID)
# 
# anti_join_1 <- anti_join(nest_IDs_preferences, nest_IDs_emergence) # IDs in preferences not in emergence
# anti_join_2 <- anti_join(nest_IDs_emergence, nest_IDs_preferences) # IDs in emergence not in preferences

# IDs in preferences but not in emergence:
# listing the reasons for discrepencies: 
# cell not completed (abandoned or just end cap and inner wall), thus nothing to emerge: 
  # anti_join_1: 43_11a, 43_14a, 44_5a, 5_12a, 50_10a, 76_11a, 83_9b, 84_13b, 93_15b
  # anti_join_2: 16_11a, 17_7a, 7_3c, 78_17a, 84_7b
# nests eaten in the field by birds or insects, thus nothing to emerge: 
  # 23_15a, 24_15a, 26_10a, 31_3a, 32_7a, 5_9a, 59_16a, 7_16a, 7_17b, 81_12b, 81_16b, 81_5a
# nests without emergence data. Unclear why, perhaps not recorded or their nest was too moldy: 
  # anti_join_1: 1_16a, 17_1b, 24_9a, 25_11a, 3_13b, 30_11b, 42_2b, 43_11b, 43_4a, 49_4b, 59_4b, 6_9b, 67_16a, 71_14a, 71_2a, 71_4a
  # anti_join_2: 15_4a, 16_1a, 17_18a, 17_9a, 2_18a, 25_16b, 25_1a, 25_4a, 30_7a, 35_8a, 36_3b, 59_4a, 6_17a, 7_4a, 8_12a, 9_9b
# nests that are mislabelled (exist in emergence data but not preferences): 13_15a, 43_3a, 6_10a, 18_8b

# remove the mislabelled nests
emerg_and_pref <- emerg_and_pref %>% filter(Nest_ID != '13_15a' & Nest_ID != '43_3a' & Nest_ID != '6_10a' & Nest_ID != '25_16b')


# bee_choice now has some duplicates after merging into emerg_and_pref, so make the duplicates NA
emerg_and_pref <- emerg_and_pref %>%
  group_by(Nest_ID) %>% 
  arrange(Nest_ID, Date) %>%
  mutate(Bee_choice = if_else(row_number() == min(which(Bee_choice == 1)), 1, NA)) %>%
  ungroup() # ignore warnings about using min() on NAs


# numbers of new nests 
sum(preferences$Bee_choice, na.rm = TRUE)  # 306, which includes the nests with only inner walls

table(preferences %>% 
        filter(Bee_choice == 1) %>% 
        pull(Contains_cells)) # 260, this includes only Megachile and Osmia nests that have at least 1 cell, and 46 that don't include cells
# check that there are no duplicates of contains_cells to make sure there are truly 261 new nests
preferences %>%
  filter(Bee_choice == 1) %>%
  group_by(Nest_ID) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(Contains_cells) > 1) %>%
  ungroup() # 0
# number of nests from emergence data
length(unique(emergence$Nest_ID)) # 248 

# are any of the Statuses NA?
sum(is.na(emerg_and_pref$Status)) 



## Making values consistent for throughout the time the nest is in the trapnest

# emerg_and_pref should have the values for number_of_cells and cumulative_par(_max) for only the dates with activity. The loop will make those values consistent throughout the time the nest is in the trapnest


## Loop 1 for making the cumulative_par_max value for the duration the nest is in the trapnest 

# make sure data is arranged chronologically
emerg_and_pref <- emerg_and_pref %>% arrange(Nest_ID, Date)
# initiate new column, then fill it in
emerg_and_pref$Cumulative_par_V2 <- emerg_and_pref$Cumulative_par_max 

# loop takes too long to do at once, so remove all empty and pseudo, then adding back in after. Tested this code at the bottom chucnk called Example Code
emerg_and_pref_excluded <- emerg_and_pref %>% filter(Status != 'empty' & Status != 'pseudo') # excluding empty and pseudo

### START
for(i in 1:nrow(emerg_and_pref_excluded)){
  nestID <- emerg_and_pref_excluded$Nest_ID[i] # focal nest for i-th row
  dt <- emerg_and_pref_excluded$Date[i] # date for i-th row
  allprev <- emerg_and_pref_excluded %>% filter(Nest_ID == nestID & Date <= dt) %>% pull(Cumulative_par_max) # all previous parasite counts for that focal nest
  
  check1 <- !all(is.na(allprev))
  check2 <- !emerg_and_pref_excluded$Status[i] %in% c('empty', 'pseudo') 

  if(check1 & check2){
    emerg_and_pref_excluded$Cumulative_par_V2[i] <- max(allprev, na.rm = T)
  }
} ### END


# bind back together
emerg_and_pref_include <- emerg_and_pref %>% filter(Status == 'empty' | Status == 'pseudo') # include empty and pseudo 
emerg_and_pref_v2 <- rbind(emerg_and_pref_excluded, emerg_and_pref_include) # 39,756
emerg_and_pref_v2 <- emerg_and_pref_v2 %>% arrange(Nest_ID, Date)
# remove unnecessary columns
emerg_and_pref_v2 <- ungroup(emerg_and_pref_v2)
emerg_and_pref_v2 <- emerg_and_pref_v2 %>% select(-Cumulative_par, -Cumulative_par_max)
# rename column and df

## Making the active period
# Wasn't working in a loop or even a single ifelse statement, so broke it up

  # Step 1: ifelse #
# criteria: within Nest_ID, starts with Bee_choice being 1, ends with anything containing 'end cap'

# make column to say if it contains 'end cap' or not
nesting_0$End_cap <- grepl('end cap', nesting_0$Status)
# make column to say if it's sealed (by containing an end cap)
nesting_0 <- nesting_0 %>% mutate(Sealed = ifelse(is.na(Bee_choice) & End_cap == TRUE | Bee_choice == 1 & End_cap == TRUE, 'sealed',
                                                ifelse(Bee_choice == 0 | is.na(Bee_choice) & Status == 'pseudo', 'NA_',
                                                       ifelse(Bee_choice == 1 & End_cap == FALSE, 'not sealed', 'leftover'))))

# inspecting to see if it worked
# insp_sealed <- nesting_0 %>% filter(Sealed == 'sealed') # yes
# insp_not_sealed <- nesting_0 %>% filter(Sealed == 'not sealed') # great
# insp_end_cap_T <- nesting_0 %>% filter(End_cap == TRUE) # wonderful
# insp_end_cap_F <- nesting_0 %>% filter(End_cap == FALSE) # amazing

  # Step 2: Loop 3 #

# arrange data chronologically
nesting_0 <- nesting_0 %>% arrange(Nest_ID, Date)
# use 7_3b for ex, is not sealed, NA, sealed, NA, want to make 7_3b not sealed, not sealed, sealed, sealed.
# use 7_8a for ex to see if multiple rows (three NAs) all say not sealed
# initiate new column, then fill it in
nesting_0$Sealed_V2 <- nesting_0$Sealed 

# loop takes too long to do at once, so remove all empty and pseudo, then adding back in after.
nesting_0_exclude <- nesting_0 %>% filter(Status != 'empty' & Status != 'pseudo') # excluding empty and pseudo

### START
for(i in 1:nrow(nesting_0_exclude)){
  nestID <- nesting_0_exclude$Nest_ID[i] # focal nest for i-th row
  dt <- nesting_0_exclude$Date[i] # date for i-th row
  allprev <- nesting_0_exclude %>% filter(Nest_ID == nestID & Date <= dt) %>% pull(Sealed_V2) # all sealed statuses for that focal nest
  
  check1 <- !all(is.na(allprev))

  if(check1 & check2){
    nesting_0_exclude$Sealed_V2[i] <- max(allprev, na.rm = T)
  }
} ### END


# bind back together
nesting_0_include <- nesting_0 %>% filter(Status == 'empty' | Status == 'pseudo') # include empty and pseudo 
nesting_0 <- rbind(nesting_0_exclude, nesting_0_include) 
nesting_0 <- nesting_0 %>% arrange(Nest_ID, Date)

# inspect
inspect_parasite_loop_3 <- nesting_0 %>% filter(Status != 'empty' & Status != 'pseudo') 

# several rows to manually fix: nest IDs 5_9a, 5_18a, 7_16a, 7_17b, 23_15a, 24_15a, 24_18a, 26_10a, 31_3a, 32_9a, 32_7a, 59_16a, 81_12b, 81_16b, 81_5a were all eaten at some point by birds or insects, so they appear as sealed or not sealed, then should again appear as NA (because they become empty), I will manually override these
# find these by sorting by Status then Sealed

# if the Nest_ID == any of those eaten nests above, then say NA_, otherwise say Sealed_02
nesting_0 <- nesting_0 %>%
  mutate(
    Sealed_V3 = ifelse(
      Status == 'empty' & Nest_ID %in% c('5_9a', '5_18a', '7_16a', '7_17b', '23_15a', '24_15a', '24_18a', '26_10a', '31_3a', '32_9a', '32_7a', '59_16a', '81_12b', '81_16b', '81_5a'),
      'NA_',
      Sealed_V2
    )
  )

# clean up df
nesting_cells <- nesting_0 %>% select(Site, Subsite, Trapnest, Treatment, Cavity_size, Cavity_number, Straw_ID, Nest_ID, Cell_number, Cell_ID, Cell_position, Date, Cell_occupant, Species_or_subtype, Cell_parasitized, Cumulative_par, Number_of_cells, Filled_length_mm, Straw_length_mm, Cavity_ID, Status, Contains_cells, Occupant, Good_days, Bee_choice, Available_post, New_nests_os, New_nests_meg, Osmia_ps, Osmia_no_ps, Meg_ps, Meg_no_ps, Osmia_ps_prior, Osmia_no_ps_prior, Meg_ps_prior, Meg_no_ps_prior, Osmia_ps_no_iw, Osmia_no_ps_no_iw, Meg_ps_no_iw, Meg_no_ps_no_iw, New_nests_sum, Available_cavities_prior, Sealed_V3)
# rename and fix NAs
nesting_cells <- rename(nesting_cells, Sealed = Sealed_V3)
nesting_cells$Sealed <- replace(nesting_cells$Sealed, nesting_cells$Sealed == 'NA_', NA)

# nesting_cells is the nesting data with cell-level observations


## Make column to say nest is parasitized or not, binary

nesting_cells <- nesting_cells %>% mutate(Nest_parasitized = ifelse(is.na(Cumulative_par), NA, 
                                                   ifelse(Cumulative_par == 0, 'not parasitized',
                                                          ifelse(Cumulative_par >= 1, 'parasitized', 'leftover'))))

# some have NAs
# if its an inner wall only, say not parasitized 
nesting_cells <- nesting_cells %>%
  group_by(Nest_ID) %>%   
  mutate(
    after_inner_wall = cumsum(Status == "inner wall"),
    before_cells = cumsum(grepl("cell", Status, ignore.case = TRUE)),

    Nest_parasitized_v2 = case_when(
      is.na(Nest_parasitized) & Status == "inner wall" ~ "not_parasitized",
      Status == "no change" & after_inner_wall > 0 & before_cells == 0 ~ "not_parasitized",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# some still have NAs for Nest_parasitized
# nesting_cells_NA_par <- nesting_cells %>% filter(!is.na(Occupant) & Occupant != 'none' & Status != 'pseudo' & is.na(Nest_parasitized) & is.na(Nest_parasitized_v2))
# all the ones that are missing for some reason (eaten, only 1 cell, no emergence data)

# combine and rename Nest_parasitized columns


nesting_cells <- nesting_cells %>% mutate(Nest_parasitized_v3 = coalesce(Nest_parasitized, Nest_parasitized_v2))
nesting_cells <- nesting_cells %>% select(-Nest_parasitized, -Nest_parasitized_v2)
nesting_cells <- nesting_cells %>% rename(Nest_parasitized = Nest_parasitized_v3)

 # Megachile

table(parasite_bin_meg$Nest_parasitized)
```

```{r Parasite_Wrangling_for_Models}
# This chunk is to make columns needed for the models

# nesting df: nest-level, used to calculate trapnest summaries
# nesting_cell df: cell-level observations
# Par_nests_unsealed: number of parasitized unsealed nests per trapnest - date combo
# Par_total: total count of parasitized cells in a trapnest

# will have to make df with only nest-level observations to make summaries, then bind back together for cell-level models 
nesting_1 <- distinct(nesting_cells, Date, Nest_ID, .keep_all= TRUE) # for nest-level 
# remove cell-level columns
nesting_1 <- select(nesting_1, -Cell_ID, -Cell_parasitized, -Cell_number)


## Count the number of unsealed nests
# for the model 9 predictor variables, I need all nests including pseudo (sealed and unsealed), all nests excluding pseudo (sealed and unsealed), which I already have (Osmia_ps_no_iw, etc) and only unsealed nests (and no pseudo nests are unsealed), which I calculate here. 
# Because I'm looking at parasites, I need the total values, not the prior values. E.g., how many existing nests are there in a trapnest when a parasite decides to lay an egg. So, there's no focal nest that would be excluded for models from the parasites perspective

# make column to count number of unsealed nests for conspecifics 
# Osmia
unsealed_summary_os <- nesting_1 %>% 
  filter(Occupant == 'osmia' & Contains_cells == 1) %>% 
  group_by(Trapnest, Date) %>% 
  summarise(Sum_unsealed_os_no_iw = sum(Active_bin, na.rm = T)) 
# Megachile
unsealed_summary_meg <- nesting_1 %>% 
  filter(Occupant == 'megachile' & Contains_cells == 1) %>% 
  group_by(Trapnest, Date) %>% 
  summarise(Sum_unsealed_meg_no_iw = sum(Active_bin, na.rm = T)) 

nesting_1 <- full_join(nesting_1, unsealed_summary_os)
nesting_1 <- full_join(nesting_1, unsealed_summary_meg)


## Make data frame for cell-level observations
nesting_cells_os_0 <- nesting_cells %>% filter(!is.na(Cell_ID))

# merge summary with new columns we made for models for preferences of parasite (excludes inner wall only) and bees (includes inner wall only)
length(unique(nesting_cells_os_0$Cell_ID)) # 716 cells, so we need a df of that length
nesting_cells_os_0 <- inner_join(nesting_cells_os_0, unsealed_summary_os)

nesting_cells_os_0[duplicated(nesting_cells_os_0$Cell_ID),] ### CHECK - I think I fixed this, April 10th


# ## Make column to say the last cell or not

#   group_by(Nest_ID) %>% 
#   slice(which.max(Cell_number)) 
# length(unique(only_last_cell_os$Nest_ID)) # checking length is all unique nest IDs
# # remove last cells from the main df

## Sum the number of parasitized cells and not
nesting_cells_os_sum <- nesting_cells_os_0 %>% 
  group_by(Date, Nest_ID) %>%
```

```{r Detectable_and_No_Detectable_Parasites}

### do the same with megachile once they emerge

### CHECK - April 24th 2024, NAs for parasites are not counted for either DP or NDP. How should NAs be counted?

### CHECK - are there instances where the nest itself is parasitized the first day its built, meaning the data would say theres 1 parasite in the trapnest but its actually 0 when it first nested because the focal nest itself is parasitized?

# In order to measure nesting preferences of bees to see if affected by parasites, I need to separate the nests with detectable parasites (DP) from the nests with no detectable parasites (NDP), see the table above
# this is about to get messy, so I'm making a smaller df 
nesting_2 <- nesting_1 %>% select(Trapnest, Date, Nest_ID, Status, Occupant, Bee_choice, New_nests_os, New_nests_meg, Osmia_ps:Meg_no_ps, Nest_parasitized, Active_bin)  

# first I make the columns with the total numbers for DP and NDP and NDP with pseudo nests, then I need to calculate the number of those three columns prior to the new bees nesting there. So if there was 1 or more new nests in DP or NDP(_ps), I calculate (total nests in that group - new nests) + (n-1)/2 for the group that the new nest is a part of. If there's new nests for the other group (e.g., new DP nest, but from the new NDP nest perspective), we do (total nests in that group - 1/2 * new nests).

# making a small df to make sure it works
# testing_36 <- nesting_2 %>% filter(Trapnest == 'trapnest_36' & Date == '2023-06-04') 


# Step 1) Making nests with total detectable parasite (DP) nests

## Count the number of unsealed parasitized nests for trapnest-date combo
# first, count the parasizited and unsealed
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(Par_and_unsealed_os = ifelse(Occupant == 'osmia' & Active_bin == 1 & Nest_parasitized == 'parasitized', 1, 0))

# having with and without inner wall doesn't matter because we're using these to count number of unsealed parasitized nests, and there are no cases where parasites occur with only inner walls

# then sum by trapnest - date combo
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>%
  group_by(Date, Trapnest) %>%
  mutate(DP_os_post = sum(Par_and_unsealed_os, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()
# DP_nests_os: number of nests that are unsealed and are parasitized, during my visit (totals including all new nests)


# Step 2) Making nests with total no detectable parasites without pseudo (NDP) nests

# first, count unsealed and not parasitized
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(No_par_and_unsealed_os = ifelse(Occupant == 'osmia' & Active_bin == 1 & Nest_parasitized == 'not parasitized' | Occupant == 'osmia' & Active_bin == 1 & Status == 'inner wall', 1, 0))

# second, count sealed, regardless of parasites
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(Sealed_os = ifelse(Occupant == 'osmia' & Active_bin == 0, 1, 0))

# thirdy, sum by trapnest - date combo
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>%
  group_by(Date, Trapnest) %>%
  mutate(NDP_os_post = sum(No_par_and_unsealed_os, na.rm=TRUE) + sum(Sealed_os, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()
# NDP_nests_os: number of nests that are unsealed and not parasitized, or sealed, during my visit (totals including all new nests)


# Step 3) Making nests with total no detectable parasites with pseudo (NDP_ps) 

# already have the count of unsealed and not parasitized (No_par_and_unsealed_os)

# second, count sealed, including pseudo
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(Sealed_os_ps = ifelse(Occupant == 'osmia' & Active_bin == 0 | Occupant == 'osmia' & Status == 'pseudo', 1, 0))

# thirdy, sum by trapnest - date combo
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>%
  group_by(Date, Trapnest) %>%
  mutate(NDP_ps_os_post = sum(No_par_and_unsealed_os, na.rm=TRUE) + sum(Sealed_os_ps, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()
# NDP_ps_os_post: number of nests that are unsealed and not parasitized, or sealed, including pseudo, during my visit (totals including all new nests)

# remove columns I don't need
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% select(-Par_and_unsealed_os, -No_par_and_unsealed_os, -Sealed_os, -Sealed_os_ps)


# Step 4) Make nests with the number of new nests for DP

 # DP 
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(DP_os_new = ifelse(Bee_choice == 1 & Occupant == 'osmia' & Active_bin == 1 & Nest_parasitized == 'parasitized', 1, 0))

nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>%
  group_by(Date, Trapnest) %>%
  mutate(DP_os_new_nests = sum(DP_os_new, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()
# DP_os_new_nests: sum of the new DP nests for trapnest - date combination


# Step 5) Make nests with the number of new nests for NDP (and NDP_ps, since no pseudo nests are ever new nests)

# first, count unsealed and no parasites
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(NDP_1_os_new = ifelse(Bee_choice == 1 & Occupant == 'osmia' & Active_bin == 1 & Nest_parasitized == 'not parasitized' | Bee_choice == 1 & Occupant == 'osmia' & Status == 'inner wall', 1, 0))
# second, sealed
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(NDP_2_os_new = ifelse(Bee_choice == 1 & Occupant == 'osmia' & Active_bin == 0, 1, 0))

nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>%
  group_by(Date, Trapnest) %>%
  mutate(NDP_os_new_nests = sum(NDP_1_os_new, na.rm=TRUE) + sum(NDP_2_os_new, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()
# NDP_os_new_nests: sum of the new NDP nests for trapnest - date combination


# Step 6) make the calculations for when one new nest is added 

# when there's 1 new nest, we remove 1 from the total (_post) 
# when there are no new nests, keep regular number

nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(DP_os_one = ifelse(DP_os_new_nests == 1, (DP_os_post - 1), 
                                                     ifelse(DP_os_new_nests == 0, DP_os_post, NA)))
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(NDP_os_one = ifelse(NDP_os_new_nests == 1, (NDP_os_post - 1), 
                                                     ifelse(NDP_os_new_nests == 0, NDP_os_post, NA)))
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(NDP_ps_os_one = ifelse(NDP_os_new_nests == 1, (NDP_ps_os_post - 1), 
                                                     ifelse(NDP_os_new_nests == 0, NDP_ps_os_post, NA)))

# DP_os_one: the prior value for DP_os when only 0 or 1 new nest was made 
# NDP_os_one: the prior value for NDP_os when only 0 or 1 new nest was made 
# NDP_ps_os_one: the prior value for NDP_ps_os when only 0 or 1 new nest was made 


# Step 7) make the calculations for when multiple new nests are added 

# total of DP or NDP - (1/2 * new DP or NDP nests)

nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(DP_mult_new_os = ifelse(DP_os_new_nests > 1, (DP_os_post - (1/2 * DP_os_new_nests)), NA))
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(NDP_mult_new_os = ifelse(NDP_os_new_nests > 1, (NDP_os_post - (1/2 * NDP_os_new_nests)), NA))
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(NDP_ps_mult_new_os = ifelse(NDP_os_new_nests > 1, (NDP_ps_os_post - (1/2 * NDP_os_new_nests)), NA))

# DP_mult_new_os: the average number of nests a new nests that DP or NDP nests would see. 
# NDP_mult_new_os: the average number of nests a new nests that DP or NDP nests would see. 
# NDP_ps_mult_new_os: the average number of nests a new nests that DP or NDP nests would see, when NDP includes pseudo


# Step 8) Create columns to use

# if theres 1 new nest of DP, use DP_os_one. If there's more than one new nest of DP, use DP_mult_new_os
# if theres 1 new nest of NDP, use NDP_os_one. If there's more than one new nest of NDP, use NDP_mult_new_os
# if theres 1 new nest of NDP, use NDP_ps_os_one. If there's more than one new nest of NDP, use NDP_ps_mult_new_os


nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(DP_os_prior = ifelse(DP_os_new_nests <= 1, DP_os_one,
                                                       ifelse(DP_os_new_nests > 1, DP_mult_new_os, NA)))
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(NDP_os_prior = ifelse(NDP_os_new_nests <= 1, NDP_os_one,
                                                       ifelse(NDP_os_new_nests > 1, NDP_mult_new_os, NA)))
nesting_2 <- nesting_2 %>% mutate(NDP_ps_os_prior = ifelse(NDP_os_new_nests <= 1, NDP_ps_os_one,
                                                       ifelse(NDP_os_new_nests > 1, NDP_ps_mult_new_os, NA)))


# # testing out some instances 
# testing_36_June <- nesting_2 %>% filter(Trapnest == 'trapnest_36' & Date == '2023-06-04') 
# testing_36_May <- nesting_2 %>% filter(Trapnest == 'trapnest_36' & Date == '2023-05-31') 
# testing_1 <- nesting_2 %>% filter(Trapnest == 'trapnest_1' & Date == '2023-05-29') 

# take columns I want
nesting <- nesting_2 %>% select(Trapnest:New_nests_meg, DP_os_post: NDP_ps_os_post, DP_os_prior:NDP_ps_os_prior)
# join with rest of df
nesting <- left_join(nesting_1, nesting)
# remove unwanted columns again
nesting <- nesting %>% select(Trapnest, Date, Day_of_year, Site:Treatment, Filled_length_mm, Straw_length_mm, Nest_ID, Status, Sealed, Nest_parasitized, Occupant:New_nests_meg, New_nests_sum, Osmia_ps_prior:Meg_no_ps_no_iw, DP_os_post:NDP_ps_os_prior)
```

```{r Prep_for_Simulations}


## Simulate the null hypothesis that bees are treating each cavity equally, thus nesting would be based just on availability

# simulation without replacement so that if there are multiple new osmia nests, the number of available cavities goes down by one for each sequential new nest in that subsite-group combo

# create a function to simulate the distribution of nests based on the null hypothesis that bees are nesting according to available cavities 
simulate_nests <- function(avail_cavities, total_nests) {
  n <- length(avail_cavities) # number of available cavities
  nest_counts <- rep(0, n) # start with zero nests in each trapnest

  # keep as zeros is no nests are built
  if (total_nests == 0) {
    return(nest_counts)
  }

  # look through each of the new nests to be randomly assigned
  for (i in 1:total_nests) {
    if (sum(avail_cavities) == 0) break  # stop if all cavities used
    probability <- avail_cavities / sum(avail_cavities) # calculate probability proportional to the number of available cavities
    chosen <- sample(1:n, size = 1, prob = probability) # randomly choose a trapnest for the new nest based on available cavities
    nest_counts[chosen] <- nest_counts[chosen] + 1 # record it
    avail_cavities[chosen] <- avail_cavities[chosen] - 1 # reduce the number of available cavities by 1, when we apply the function the loop will run again until no new nests are left
  }
  return(nest_counts) # return the vector with how many nests were randomly assigned
}

## Apply the function

# indicate how many simulated data columns we want for the model
n_sim <- 100 

nesting_os_xs_null <- nesting_os_xs %>%
  group_by(Subsite, Date) %>%
  group_modify(~ { # simulate random nest distribution for subsite-date combo
    for (i in 1:n_sim){ # make each of the columns we indicated that we want 
    nest_counts <- simulate_nests(.x$Available_cavities_prior, sum(.x$New_nests_os)) # use available cavities as weights and sum the new nests
    .x[[paste0('Null_new_nests', i)]] <- nest_counts # make the new column
    }
    .x # return the modified group
  }
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


## Making the model part 1: Simulated data 

# run the model on each of the simulated data columns, which will create the summary outputs of each simulated data model
sim_list <- lapply(1:n_sim, function(x){
  my_formula <- paste0('Null_new_nests', x, ' ~ scale(Osmia_ps_prior) + scale(Good_days) + poly(Day_of_year,2) + Site + (1|Subsite/Trapnest)') 
  output <- glmer(as.formula(my_formula), data = nesting_os_xs_null, family = poisson)
  summary(output)
} )

# take all of the simulated coefficients
sim_coefs <- c(unlist(lapply(sim_list, function(x) {
  x$coefficients[2,1] # extract second row, first column for the estimate 
})))

# plot the simulated coefficients
hist(sim_coefs)


## Making the model part 2: Observed data 

mod_choice_consp_os_ps <- glmer(New_nests_os ~ scale(Osmia_ps_prior) + scale(Good_days) + poly(Day_of_year,2) + Site + (1|Subsite/Trapnest), data = nesting_os_xs_null, family = poisson)
summary(mod_choice_consp_os_ps)

# extract my observed coefficient
obvs_coef <- summary(mod_choice_consp_os_ps)$coefficients[2,1]

# plot my observed values with the simulated coefficients
abline(v=obvs_coef)

# range of 95%, i.e., if my observed value falls within this range, its not different from the null
quantile(sim_coefs, c(0.025, 0.975))

# Convert to dataframe
df <- data.frame(sim_coefs = sim_coefs)

ggplot(df, aes(x = sim_coefs)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = obvs_coef, color = 'red', linetype = 'dashed', size = 1) 




```
